useful: overview: the monthly pivot per direction showed at once the dead periods, the three northbound-only failures and the 2013 dip
zeros(counter=True): exact boundaries of every outage, including single whole-day dropouts and the 2015-04-24 morning reset
channels: showed the 2012-07-08 bursts sitting in a single record (410 in one of four)
compare: Harbour Bridge and King St stayed flat through the 2013 dip, so it is local
daily + weather: ruled out rain for the whole-day zeros and found exact transition days
not_useful: spikes: its 'usual' baseline is a median over the whole record, so two years of a dead northbound sensor turned every ordinary commuter peak into a 'spike'
duplicates: only flagged all-zero days inside the dead 2020-2023 period
improve: spikes: compute 'usual' from a rolling window (e.g. +/-60 days) of non-zero days, so long outages do not distort it
channels: records are listed in ID order, so they cannot be followed as channels from slot to slot; a stable channel index would let a reviewer see which sensor failed
add: a direction-ratio tracker: the daily N/S ratio with runs where it departs from its long-run level, to find one-direction sensor failures directly

summary: Kent St (E) south of Margaret St was counted by an Ecocounter (2012-2020) and, after a 5-year gap, by a Metrocount (2025-). The Ecocounter had many whole-counter outages (weeks to months of zeros, plus single dead days), two long northbound-only sensor failures (2015-02 to 2015-04 and 2016-06 to 2018-06), and a burst of phantom southbound counts on 2012-07-08; all are set missing. A 2013 dip in both directions stays uncertain, the Metrocount data looks clean, and the two counters are kept as separate series.
